channel.title: BSV.place — Corrections and evidence briefs
channel.description: Material revisions and evidence-first responses to common BSV objections.

item.title: A Merkle Proof Is a Receipt, Not a Backup
item.description: What Bitcoin proves about transaction inclusion, order, and integrity—and what builders must still preserve, index, explain, and make portable.

item.description: Published a source-led guide to Merkle proofs, record availability, application layers, and the recovery evidence builders should ship.

item.title: Independent static publication established
item.description: BSV.place now uses static external hosting, a protected custom domain, and enforced HTTPS to keep the reference available independently of application infrastructure.

item.title: Does the BSV case depend on Craig Wright being Satoshi?
item.description: No identity claim is required. Software, network rules, economics, and actual use should stand or fall on inspectable evidence of their own.

item.title: Is BSV captured by a small set of institutions and patrons?
item.description: Concentration is a legitimate dependency question. It should be answered with an inventory of authority, funding, code ownership, operators, and replaceability—not a decentralization slogan.

item.title: How should a serious person respond to the “scam” or “cult” label?
item.description: A label is not a technical analysis, but it often points to a valid proof problem: were people sold allegiance and price stories instead of working utility and disclosed risk?

item.title: Where are the users?
item.description: The public adoption proof remains thinner than the technical inventory. That gap should be measured, not covered with anecdotes or raw transaction counts.

item.title: Does anything economically need BSV?
item.description: Correct: a cheap transaction is a component, not a product. The case must be a workflow where public proofs, tiny payments, or portable signed records change user value or unit economics.

item.title: Does building on BSV create unacceptable reputational risk?
item.description: That is a real commercial risk affecting hiring, partnerships, fundraising, and distribution. It can be reduced by clean-room product framing and evidence, not denied.

item.title: Is BSV “really Bitcoin”?
item.description: Chain identity is partly historical and social. For a product decision, compare implemented design goals and current rules instead of demanding agreement on a purity title.

item.title: Is “Satoshi's Vision” a defensible description?
item.description: The phrase is defensible only when defined narrowly as a set of design goals. It should not imply that every current governance choice appears in, or is compelled by, the whitepaper.

item.title: Can nodes reject a longer proof-of-work chain and still claim Bitcoin rules?
item.description: This is a serious protocol-governance dispute. Proof of work coordinates valid history; the hard questions are who defines validity, what policies can change it, and how operators learn the rules.

item.title: Can BSV freeze or reassign coins?
item.description: The published governance surface is real and consequential. It should be evaluated as a disputed-property recovery tradeoff—not denied or confused with ordinary wallet authority.

item.title: Does the BSV Association function as a central authority?
item.description: BSV does include explicit institutional governance. The defensible question is whether its scope, checks, transparency, and fit are acceptable for a use case.

item.title: Do delistings and weak liquidity make BSV unusable?
item.description: Liquidity and service access are real operational dependencies for some products and nearly incidental for others. They must be tested at decision time.

item.title: Do price and “flippening” narratives invalidate the builder case?
item.description: They do not invalidate a working product, but they contaminate its credibility and attract the wrong success metrics.

item.title: Why does BSV discourse so often feel tribal or abusive?
item.description: Factional tone is a real credibility and distribution cost. Friendly hostility does not become helpful because it comes from an ally.

item.title: What can a skeptical person actually try?
item.description: That request is an opportunity. Every capability claim should lead to a bounded, reproducible path with expected output and honest failure handling.

item.title: Is BSV too complicated to build on?
item.description: The cognitive-load objection is valid. A newcomer should start with one user outcome and a high-level API, then reveal lower layers only when they solve a real problem.

item.title: Is BRC-100 real interoperability or one vendor's interface?
item.description: That is the right proof standard. BRC-100 is a substantial public interface; interoperability depends on conforming independent implementations and observable compatibility.

item.title: Can users actually leave a wallet, app, or overlay?
item.description: Correct. Portability is an operational property demonstrated by export, import, discovery, replacement, and recovery—not inferred from public keys or blockchain storage.

item.title: Is BSV scaling real, or a datacenter marketing claim?
item.description: BSV has a coherent large-block architecture and public Teranode source. Capacity, independent reproduction, production behavior, demand, and operator diversity remain separate claims.

item.title: What do hashpower and reorganization history mean for BSV security?
item.description: Hash economics, transaction validity, confirmation policy, topology, monitoring, and governance response are separate security layers. None should be hand-waved.

item.title: Why have so many funded BSV projects disappeared?
item.description: Failed projects are normal; missing accountability is not. Judge a current ecosystem by maintained products, user outcomes, and transparent status—not by cumulative launch announcements.

item.title: Is BSV just a cheap database for spam?
item.description: This is a genuine design-priority disagreement. Cheap public blockspace can support proofs and signed records while imposing permanent-resource and privacy costs.

item.title: Can miners, the chain, or an app sign as me or read my private data?
item.description: These are different authority layers. Network recovery can affect accepted coin ownership without automatically granting a user's signing keys, decryption keys, certificates, or app permissions.

item.title: Does Project Babbage depend too heavily on the BSV rail?
item.description: BSV is the current rail, so failure is a material dependency. Portability claims must distinguish reusable interfaces and user data from BSV-specific transactions, proofs, licenses, and services.
